detail.body:
## Purpose

Add a native Triton per-token FP8 scaled-MM linear backend, with tuned configurations for Radeon AI PRO R9700 / gfx1201. Select it with `--linear-backend triton` for dynamic per-token activation scales and per-channel weight scales.

Related: [#60672](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60672), which enables the existing AITER per-token FP8 backend. This PR provides the vLLM-native implementation and keeps its tuning configurations in vLLM.
this fixes the regression in #57838 without disabling the working but slower `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` in #57861

The per-token FP8 runtime lives in `linear/scaled_mm/triton.py`, reuses the existing shared Triton scaled-MM kernel, and supports BF16/FP16 output, bias, compiled dynamic shapes, and graph replay. Tile and scheduling choices live in configuration files, with guarded fallbacks for unsupported layouts and unmeasured shapes. The per-token backend is registered only for ROCm and requires `current_platform.supports_fp8()`.

## Validation

Test environment: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / gfx1201, Torch 2.13 with ROCm 10, and Triton 3.8. Model: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic`.

Validation covers operator correctness, backend selection, compiled execution, graph replay, strided scales, and tile/layout boundaries. Kernel comparisons use identical FP8 operands and scales against Torch RowWise, with quantization excluded from the timings. Serving performance compares Torch RowWise and native Triton with the same attention backend and AITER linear disabled.

```bash
uv run pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_triton_scaled_mm.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py \
  -k 'not rocm_compressed_tensors_w8a8'
```

Operator and backend-selection tests, rerun after simplifying the tests: **152 passed, 1 deselected** (INT8 checkpoint smoke test excluded by the command above). Pre-commit checks passed. The simplification removes launch-recording fixtures, exact tuning-policy assertions, and redundant large-shape cases while retaining numerical correctness, compiled dynamic shapes, graph replay with mutated inputs/scales, strided scales, and operand-boundary coverage. The shared Triton kernel and tuning configurations are unchanged from the benchmarked version. The fresh serving comparison below completed **480 successful requests**, with no errors or incomplete requests.

Benchmark correctness validation uses `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=atol=1e-2`. **44 cases** (11 installed shapes × M=1/64/256/2048) passed for both heuristic and tuned paths. BF16/FP16 smoke checks passed, and injected mismatches and non-finite outputs were rejected.

```bash
uv run benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py \
  --shapes 3840,2048 3840,4096 3840,7680 3840,8192 3840,15360 \
    4096,3840 5120,3840 8192,3840 9216,3840 15360,3840 30720,3840 \
  --m 1 64 256 2048 --validate-only --rep-ms 1 --rounds 1 \
  --output-dir fp8-validation
```

### Accuracy validation

GSM8K accuracy was evaluated with vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` on the full **1,319-question** test set: **5-shot**, greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, seed 42), chat completions with thinking disabled, a 1,024-token output limit, and 32 concurrent requests. Both runs used **TP2**, **FP8 KV cache**, and default serving settings, changing only `--linear-backend`. Attention was selected automatically (`TRITON_ATTN`); no attention or AITER environment override was used. Evaluated PR commit: `bf64ce9836f2`.

| Backend | Correct / questions | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Torch RowWise | 1,255 / 1,319 | 95.15% | 0 |
| Native Triton | 1,251 / 1,319 | 94.84% | 0 |

Triton minus Torch RowWise: **-0.30 percentage points**. In the paired comparison, Triton answered 13 questions correctly that Torch missed, and missed 17 questions Torch answered correctly. Triton answered 4 fewer questions correctly in this single run. All **2,638 evaluation requests** completed successfully; 0 responses reached the output-token limit. These results cover this model and GSM8K configuration; other models and platforms need separate evaluation.

This accuracy comparison uses default attention. The TP1 serving performance measurements below use explicitly selected `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`.

To reproduce, start each server separately, using `torch` for the baseline and `triton` for the candidate:

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --linear-backend torch
```

Run the evaluator against each server:

```bash
uv run tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --use-chat-completions \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42 \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 \
  --request-timeout-seconds 7200 \
  --save-results gsm8k-results.json
```

### Serving commands

Install vLLM from this PR. Run each configuration separately on the same GPU.

**TP1 baseline (Torch RowWise)**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --linear-backend torch
```

**TP1 native Triton**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --linear-backend triton
```

### Workload

Benchmark with GuideLLM 0.7.3:

- 8 turns.
- 2048 configured prompt tokens per turn.
- 512 output tokens per request.
- 1/2/4/8 streams with 8/16/32/64 requests.

### Results

<!-- native-triton-serving-results:start -->
End-to-end TP1 serving: Torch RowWise versus native Triton, using the commands above. Two fresh-server runs per backend use reversed order. Each baseline/candidate pair stays on the same GPU, with empty compilation caches for each server. All four profiles reach their configured concurrency and preserve all eight turns.

Each cell shows **Torch RowWise → native Triton (percentage change)**. Output tok/s is the mean per-request output rate (output tokens divided by end-to-end request latency). Absolute measurements are kept separate for the two same-GPU pairs. The summary percentages below are geometric means of their Triton/RowWise ratios. Every successful request, including warmup/cooldown and first-use requests, is included. Positive output-rate changes and negative TTFT/E2E changes improve performance.

| Pair | Streams | Mean output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 28.09 → 32.62 (**+16.1%**) | 915 → 1,153 (+26.0%) | 18.24 → 15.74 (**−13.7%**) |
| 1 | 2 | 26.82 → 31.41 (**+17.1%**) | 1,149 → 1,139 (**−0.9%**) | 19.10 → 16.32 (**−14.6%**) |
| 1 | 4 | 24.79 → 28.80 (**+16.1%**) | 1,850 → 1,800 (**−2.7%**) | 20.70 → 17.84 (**−13.8%**) |
| 1 | 8 | 20.88 → 23.91 (**+14.5%**) | 2,911 → 2,823 (**−3.0%**) | 24.65 → 21.56 (**−12.5%**) |
| 2 | 1 | 28.09 → 32.70 (**+16.4%**) | 925 → 1,135 (+22.7%) | 18.24 → 15.71 (**−13.9%**) |
| 2 | 2 | 26.64 → 31.38 (**+17.8%**) | 1,171 → 1,123 (**−4.1%**) | 19.23 → 16.33 (**−15.1%**) |
| 2 | 4 | 24.57 → 28.59 (**+16.4%**) | 1,776 → 1,673 (**−5.8%**) | 20.88 → 17.97 (**−13.9%**) |
| 2 | 8 | 20.65 → 23.60 (**+14.3%**) | 3,011 → 2,872 (**−4.6%**) | 24.93 → 21.88 (**−12.2%**) |

Mean per-request output rate improves by **14.4–17.4%** across the four stream levels. Mean request latency falls by **12.4–14.8%**. Mean TTFT increases at 1 stream (**+24.4%**). First-use requests remain included in the measurements.

These are synthetic-text serving measurements. GSM8K accuracy is evaluated separately above at TP2 with default attention. Multimodal inputs and performance on other architectures remain to be validated.

[Full comparison, per-turn charts, raw results, and provenance](https://github.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm-bench-collection/blob/4f92502e7036abbcc535daac8dda4147fe41b8ec/comparisons/gfx1201/gemma-4-12b-fp8-dynamic/rocm10-native-triton-pr61091-tp1-20261012-v1/README.md).

![Mean per-request output rate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm-bench-collection/4f92502e7036abbcc535daac8dda4147fe41b8ec/comparisons/gfx1201/gemma-4-12b-fp8-dynamic/rocm10-native-triton-pr61091-tp1-20261012-v1/serving_tps.png)

![Mean time to first token](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm-bench-collection/4f92502e7036abbcc535daac8dda4147fe41b8ec/comparisons/gfx1201/gemma-4-12b-fp8-dynamic/rocm10-native-triton-pr61091-tp1-20261012-v1/serving_ttft.png)

![Mean request latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm-bench-collection/4f92502e7036abbcc535daac8dda4147fe41b8ec/comparisons/gfx1201/gemma-4-12b-fp8-dynamic/rocm10-native-triton-pr61091-tp1-20261012-v1/serving_e2e.png)

<!-- native-triton-serving-results:end -->

## Duplicate-work check

Reviewed #57838 and related open PRs. #60672 enables AITER, #57861 changes the Torch fallback, #58238 adds a HIP kernel, and #60903 optimizes activation quantization. This PR adds the native Triton scaled-MM backend.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used for implementation, validation, and PR preparation. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing the complete diff.

@@ -0,0 +1,406 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tune or validate native per-token FP8 GEMM with transposed weights.
+
+Example: .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_per_token_fp8.py
+    --shapes 4096,3840 3840,4096 --output-dir /tmp/per-token-tuning
+
+Use --out-dtype float16 to tune FP16 output, --m to select batch sizes,
+--resume to continue an interrupted sweep, or --validate-only to compare
+installed configs against the default heuristic through the runtime custom op.
+Use --group-m and --n-stripe to search scheduling choices, and
+--unmasked-loads to request complete aligned operand loads.
+
+Configs are written to output-dir/configs. Copy them to
+vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs after validation.
+Tuning and independent finalist measurements use GPU graphs and hot operands;
+quantization, attention, and tensor-parallel communication are excluded.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+import random
+import statistics
+import time
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.triton_scaled_mm import (  # noqa: E501
+    triton_scaled_mm,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
+    get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config,
+    get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config_filename,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import get_device_name_as_file_name
+
+
+def candidates(group_m, n_stripe, unmasked_loads):
+    keys = (
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_M",
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_N",
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_K",
+        "num_warps",
+        "num_stages",
+        "GROUP_M",
+        "N_STRIPE",
+    )
+    return [
+        dict(zip(keys, values), UNMASKED_LOADS=unmasked_loads)
+        for values in itertools.product(
+            (16, 32, 64, 128),
+            (32, 64, 128),
+            (64, 128, 256),
+            (4, 8),
+            (1, 2, 3),
+            group_m,
+            n_stripe,
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def call(a, b, sa, sb, config=None, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    kwargs = {}
+    if config is not None:
+        kwargs = {
+            "use_heuristic": False,
+            "block_size_m": config["BLOCK_SIZE_M"],
+            "block_size_n": config["BLOCK_SIZE_N"],
+            "block_size_k": config["BLOCK_SIZE_K"],
+            "num_warps": config["num_warps"],
+            "num_stages": config["num_stages"],
+            "group_m": config.get("GROUP_M", 1),
+            "n_stripe": config.get("N_STRIPE", 0),
+            "unmasked_loads": bool(config.get("UNMASKED_LOADS", False)),
+        }
+    return triton_scaled_mm(a, b, sa, sb, out_dtype, **kwargs)
+
+
+def reference(a, w, sa, sb):
+    rows = torch.linspace(0, a.shape[0] - 1, min(a.shape[0], 64), device=a.device)
+    cols = torch.linspace(0, w.shape[0] - 1, min(w.shape[0], 128), device=w.device)
+    rows, cols = rows.long().unique(), cols.long().unique()
+    ref = (a[rows].float() @ w[cols].float().t()) * sa[rows] * sb[cols].t()
+    return rows, cols, ref
+
+
+def check(output, ref, rows, cols):
+    for chunk in output.reshape(-1).split(16 * 1024 * 1024):
+        if not torch.isfinite(chunk).all().item():
+            raise ValueError("Non-finite output")
+    sample = output[rows[:, None], cols[None, :]].float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(sample, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+    error = ((sample - ref).square().mean() / ref.square().mean()).sqrt().item()
+    return error
+
+
+def bench(fn, rep_ms):
+    benchmark = (
+        triton.testing.do_bench
+        if current_platform.is_xpu()
+        else triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph
+    )
+    return 1000 * benchmark(fn, rep=rep_ms, return_mode="median")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--shapes", nargs="+", required=True, help="N,K pairs")
+    parser.add_argument("--group-m", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1])
+    parser.add_argument("--n-stripe", type=int, nargs="+", default=[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--unmasked-loads", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--m", "--batch-sizes", type=int, nargs="+", default=[2**i for i in range(16)]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", "--save-path", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--out-dtype", choices=("bfloat16", "float16"), default="bfloat16"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--device", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--search-ms", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--rep-ms", type=int, default=10)
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--finalists", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--validate-only",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Benchmark installed configs through the native custom op vs heuristic",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not (current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or current_platform.is_xpu()):
+        parser.error("Requires a CUDA, ROCm, or XPU device")
+    if any(m <= 0 for m in args.m):
+        parser.error("Batch sizes must be positive")
+    out_dtype = getattr(torch, args.out_dtype)
+    run_mm = partial(call, out_dtype=out_dtype)
+    device = current_platform.device_type
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(args.device)
+    torch.set_num_threads(4)
+    shapes = sorted({tuple(map(int, s.split(","))) for s in args.shapes})
+    if any(len(shape) != 2 or min(shape) <= 0 for shape in shapes):
+        parser.error("Shapes must be positive N,K pairs")
+    cases = [(m, n, k) for n, k in shapes for m in sorted(set(args.m))]
+    if not cases:
+        parser.error("No cases to run")
+    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    result_path = args.output_dir / "results.jsonl"
+    if result_path.exists() and not args.resume:
+        raise FileExistsError("Choose a fresh output directory")
+    if any(group < 1 for group in args.group_m) or any(n < 0 for n in args.n_stripe):
+        parser.error("GROUP_M must be positive and N_STRIPE nonnegative")
+    search = (
+        []
+        if args.validate_only
+        else candidates(args.group_m, args.n_stripe, args.unmasked_loads)
+    )
+    if args.validate_only:
+        import vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.scaled_mm.triton  # noqa: F401
+    metadata = {
+        "device": str(getattr(torch, device).get_device_properties(args.device)),
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "hip": torch.version.hip,
+        "triton": triton.__version__,
+        "input_dtype": str(current_platform.fp8_dtype()),
+        "output_dtype": args.out_dtype,
+        "weight_layout": "contiguous [N,K] storage, transposed [K,N] view",
+        "method": ("event timing" if current_platform.is_xpu() else "CUDA graphs")
+        + ", hot operands, median of randomized rounds",
+        "bias": False,
+        "quantization_included": False,
+        "correctness": "all elements finite; <=64 rows x128 columns vs FP32",
+        "cases": cases,
+        "search_space": search,
+        "arguments": {
+            k: str(v) if isinstance(v, Path) else v for k, v in vars(args).items()
+        },
+        "sources": {},
+    }
+    for source in (
+        Path(__file__),
+        Path(triton_scaled_mm.__code__.co_filename),
+        Path(get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config.__code__.co_filename),
+    ):
+        metadata["sources"][str(source)] = hashlib.sha256(
+            source.read_bytes()
+        ).hexdigest()
+    checkpoints = args.output_dir / "checkpoints"
+    checkpoints.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    complete = {}
+    metadata_path = args.output_dir / "metadata.json"
+    if args.resume and metadata_path.exists():
+        old = json.loads(metadata_path.read_text())
+        for key in (
+            "device",
+            "torch",
+            "hip",
+            "triton",
+            "sources",
+            "cases",
+        ):
+            assert json.loads(json.dumps(metadata.get(key))) == old.get(key), key
+        old_args, new_args = dict(old["arguments"]), dict(metadata["arguments"])
+        old_args.pop("resume")
+        new_args.pop("resume")
+        assert old_args == new_args, "Resume arguments differ"
+        for path in checkpoints.glob("*.json"):
+            row = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            case = (row["M"], row["N"], row["K"])
+            assert case in cases and case not in complete, path
+            complete[case] = row
+        # Atomic checkpoints also recover a partially written JSONL tail.
+        result_path.write_text(
+            "".join(json.dumps(complete[c]) + "\n" for c in cases if c in complete)
+        )
+    metadata["completed_cases"] = len(complete)
+    metadata_path.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    configs = {}
+
+    def save(record):
+        name = f"M={record['M']}-N={record['N']}-K={record['K']}.json"
+        path = checkpoints / name
+        temp = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
+        temp.write_text(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+        temp.replace(path)
+        with result_path.open("a") as stream:
+            stream.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+
+    if not args.validate_only:
+        for (m, n, k), row in complete.items():
+            filename = get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config_filename(
+                n,
+                k,
+                get_device_name_as_file_name(),
+                current_platform.fp8_dtype(),
+                out_dtype,
+            )
+            configs.setdefault(filename, {})[m] = row["config"]
+        # Rebuild exports even if the interruption followed the final checkpoint.
+        folder = args.output_dir / "configs"
+        folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+        for filename, config in configs.items():
+            (folder / filename).write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=4) + "\n")
+    for index, case in enumerate(cases):
+        if case in complete:
+            continue
+        m, n, k = case
+        seed_index = index
+        torch.manual_seed(1234 + seed_index)
+        dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
+        a = (torch.randn(m, k, device=device) * 0.2).to(dtype)
+        w = (torch.randn(n, k, device=device) * 0.2).to(dtype)
+        b = w.t()
+        sa = torch.rand(m, 1, device=device) + 0.5
+        sb = torch.rand(n, 1, device=device) + 0.5
+        rows, cols, ref = reference(a, w, sa, sb)
+        if args.validate_only:
+            config = get_w8a8_per_token_fp8_config(m, n, k, dtype, out_dtype)
+            if config is None:
+                raise ValueError(f"No installed tuned config for {case}")
+            methods = {
+                "heuristic": partial(run_mm, a, b, sa, sb),
+                "tuned": partial(
+                    torch.ops.vllm.w8a8_triton_per_token_scaled_mm_func,
+                    a,
+                    b,
+                    sa,
+                    sb,
+                    out_dtype,
+                    None,
+                    True,
+                ),
+            }
+            errors = {
+                name: check(fn(), ref, rows, cols) for name, fn in methods.items()
+            }
+            timings = {name: [] for name in methods}
+            rng = random.Random(1234 + seed_index)
+            for _ in range(args.rounds):
+                names = list(methods)
+                rng.shuffle(names)
+                for name in names:
+                    timings[name].append(bench(methods[name], args.rep_ms))
+            record = {
+                "M": m,
+                "N": n,
+                "K": k,
+                "config": config,
+                "relative_rms": errors,
+                "samples_us": timings,
+                "median_us": {
+                    name: statistics.median(t) for name, t in timings.items()
+                },
+            }
+            record["speedup"] = (
+                record["median_us"]["heuristic"] / record["median_us"]["tuned"]
+            )
+            save(record)
+            print(
+                f"[{index + 1}/{len(cases)}] M={m} N={n} K={k}: "
+                f"{record['median_us']} ({record['speedup']:.3f}x)",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            methods.clear()
+            del a, w, b, sa, sb, rows, cols, ref
+            torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+            continue
+        ranked, skipped = [], []
+        order = list(search)
+        random.Random(1234 + seed_index).shuffle(order)
+        print(f"[{index + 1}/{len(cases)}] searching M={m} N={n} K={k}", flush=True)
+        for candidate in order:
+            fn = partial(run_mm, a, b, sa, sb, candidate)
+            try:
+                error = check(fn(), ref, rows, cols)

The shared `triton_scaled_mm` changes do affect existing INT8 callers, so I checked end-to-end Quark INT8 inference against the original shared implementation.

The Quark INT8 route is `QuarkW8A8Int8.apply_weights` → `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` → INT8 activation quantization → `triton_scaled_mm` → `scaled_mm_kernel`. It retains the default launch policy and skips `_get_scaled_mm_launch_policy`; the new FP8 tuning-config loader is not on this route. `_scaled_mm_tile_coords` runs as compiled Triton.

I ran [Gemma 4 12B Quark W8A8 INT8](https://huggingface.co/rajasingh012/gemma-4-12b-it-quark-w8a8-int8) on two AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs (gfx1201) with TP2, default cuda graph mode.  Both cases explicitly select the existing Triton INT8 backend. 

The run was testing using the same benchmark configs in the Pr Message above.

| Streams | Per-request output TPS change | Mean TTFT change | Mean end-to-end latency change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +0.15% | −4.70% | −0.29% |
| 2 | +0.67% | −10.06% | −0.93% |
| 4 | +0.63% | −8.72% | −1.22% |
| 8 | −1.63% | +4.86% | +2.50% |

Positive TPS changes and negative latency changes improve performance. Runtime logs confirm over 16,000 FULL graph replays in each case. Replay bypasses repeated Python wrapper/launch work inside captured regions; uncaptured prefill and other serving overhead remain.

The measured serving impact is small in this graph-enabled Quark test, with no consistent slowdown across stream levels.

For the CUDA CUTLASS path, I also inspected checkpoint/config coverage. When CUTLASS is selected, the shared wrapper uses native CUTLASS if the weight's K and N dimensions are multiples of 16. The FP8 CUTLASS linear backend also pads weights and activations to satisfy this alignment. Grouping the inspected checkpoints by architecture, size, and precision gives three distinct examples:

| Model group (representative checkpoint) | Evidence for avoiding the shared Triton fallback |
|---|---|
| [Gemma 4 12B FP8 Dynamic](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic) | Local checkpoint inspection: all 328 FP8 matrices have aligned K/N dimensions. |
| [Qwen2.5-VL 3B W8A8 INT8](https://huggingface.co/lsm0729/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8) | Published configs: quantized text-layer dimensions are aligned; vision layers are excluded from INT8. Groups the inspected 3B W8A8 and SmoothQuant variants. |
| [Qwen2.5-VL 7B W8A8 INT8](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8) | Published configs: quantized text-layer dimensions are aligned; vision layers are excluded from INT8. Groups the inspected RedHatAI, lsm0729, and zzen0008 variants. |

For these inspected models, the shared Triton changes are unlikely to affect the CUDA path through the alignment fallback. Irregular INT8 layers and irregular direct FP8 wrapper inputs can still reach Triton, but with default cuda graph capture enabled it seems the small launch overhead is negligible.

HI @amd-xavierwang the goal of this was never to avoid AITER, rather make it complementary.

We understand that AITER when tuned has better performance, but it performs worse compared to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` when untuned.
The AITER enablement at #61091 for RDNA4/3 works for tuned paths only. whenever we dont hit a tuned path it falls back to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` 

In untuned Isolated benchmarks the work here brings perf improvements at `1.10-1.30x over RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` 

For users using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1` they get both the tuned aiter implementation + this fallback benefit. 

For users not using AITER, they still get a better performance compared to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
